The analysis above overlooks known results about integrally closed monomial ideals in three variables. In fact, it is true that every integrally closed monomial ideal of height 3 in \(k[x,y,z]\) that has **four or fewer** minimal monomial generators is normal; counter‑examples to normality first appear when there are five generators. Therefore the maximal integer \(N\) that guarantees normality is \(N=4\), not \(N=3\).
